llm.summary: It's US midterm Election Day and the market is open, which means every cross-asset move today is being filtered through a political event nobody can position for cleanly. The overnight relief that drove yesterday's bounce has reversed: US strikes on Iran and a drone attack on a UAE nuclear plant pushed crude from sub-$95 back above $103-105, reviving the inflation leg of the stagflation regime just as 10-year yields press toward 5%. Gold did not work as the hedge — it fell 3% through $4,000 and briefly below $3,900 before a ~2% bounce, with silver down over 3%, a pattern that says real-rate repricing and forced deleveraging, not safe-haven demand. The AI complex is now down roughly $5tn in three weeks and hedge funds have gone underweight AI for the first time since 2023; Palantir beat and raised and fell 6% on total-contract-value deceleration, Lumentum gapped -18.6% on the Marvell deal, Amazon cancelled Nvidia DGX Spark orders, and Nvidia is forcing cloud partners to cap China at 49% of services. Apple is sinking on memory-cost inflation and is set to lose the market-cap crown — the AI hardware shortage has become an input-cost problem for everyone downstream. Meanwhile the non-AI tape is quietly excellent: Pfizer, Teva, Ferrari, DuPont, Gartner and Fiserv all raised guidance, and the average stock just beat the S&P 500 by the most since 2009. Flows confirm it — Energy 96, Health Care 94, Staples 89, Materials 84 versus Tech -58 and Comm Services -85, with Value leading Growth by 123 points, up from 99 yesterday. The portfolio's defensive-value, insurance-and-healthcare tilt is exactly where the capital is going; the risk is complacency about the consumer, where Americans now spend nearly half their budget on food and housing, the highest share in 15 years.

market_thesis.short_term: Two-sided and event-driven. The oil relief that powered yesterday is gone — US strikes on Iran and a UAE nuclear-plant drone attack put crude back above $100, which re-tightens the yield screw on everything long-duration into a 5% 10-year. Gold failing at $4,000 while oil rises is the important tell: this is not a classic risk-off, it is a deleveraging where hedges are being sold to fund margin in the AI complex. Expect the rotation to keep running rather than the index to crack — Value's lead over Growth widened from 99 to 123 points in a single session, and the average stock is beating the S&P by the most since 2009, meaning mega-cap concentration is unwinding into broad value rather than into cash. Midterm results tonight are the binary: a Democratic sweep is the scenario CNBC flags as capable of jolting stocks, and Trump DOJ election litigation raises the probability of a contested, multi-day resolution that keeps volatility elevated through the week into Friday payrolls.
market_thesis.medium_term: Stagflation 34.2 and Reflation 33.0 rising together while Goldilocks collapses to 16.1 (-13.8 trend) is the defining setup for the next few months: nominal growth holds, prices stay sticky, and the Fed is on hold with hike risk, not cut optionality — while Australia has already gone to its highest policy rate since 2008. In that world the AI capex story separates into fundable and unfundable. Nvidia extending credit, Amazon cancelling hardware orders, CoreWeave sliding on debt concerns, and Marvell's $115bn stock-funded Lumentum deal immediately destroying 18.6% of Lumentum's value are all evidence the marginal AI dollar is now priced as risk capital. Simultaneously the physical layer keeps compounding: PNW raised guidance on load growth with a $10.35bn capital plan, Samsung's Texas fab is booked by AMD and Nvidia for 2029 tools, and defense/space names (Voyager, SFC Energy) are raising. Earnings quality outside tech is the best signal in this tape — healthcare, insurance, industrials and staples are raising guidance into an environment where their multiples never inflated.
market_thesis.long_term: Energy, electrons, interconnect and healthcare delivery remain the durable claims. AI demand is real but the financing structure around it was built for a 3% long end and is being rebuilt for a 5% one; that takes years and consolidates the industry toward balance-sheet owners. Geopolitically the world is fragmenting into parallel supply chains — Nvidia's 51% non-China rule for cloud partners, AGOA removal for South Africa and Rwanda, DP World's new weekly China-Africa service, and Beijing's cross-border payment push all point to duplicated infrastructure, higher structural capex and structurally higher baseline inflation. On the household side, a 15-year high in the share of budgets going to food and housing permanently entrenches consumer bifurcation: value retail, generic/branded pharma access, and insurance-like security products take share from discretionary goods for a decade. Crypto's retail flywheel is structurally impaired after a $6.3bn state-sponsored Binance heist and $5bn of withdrawals; value migrates to regulated custody and tokenized traditional securities.

short_term: Households are reallocating toward necessity: nearly half of US budgets now go to food and housing, the highest share in 15 years, and MarketWatch is flagging three signs of an approaching consumer 'spend-pocalypse' — discretionary goods demand is the first casualty.
Investors are selling their hedges to fund their losses — gold -3% and silver -3% alongside rising oil means margin, not conviction, is setting hard-asset prices this week.

Professional money is capitulating on AI positioning rather than trimming: hedge funds went underweight AI for the first time since 2023 after a $5tn three-week drawdown, which mechanically removes the marginal buyer of dips.
Corporates are cancelling or deferring AI hardware commitments at the edges — Amazon cancelling Nvidia DGX Spark orders is a demand signal, not a supply one.

Retail attention is rotating from AI narrative to personal P&L: rising queries cluster on bitcoin price, Robinhood login/gold card and Netflix prices — people checking accounts and subscription costs, not exploring new themes.
Crypto users are voting with withdrawals — $5bn pulled from Binance on reopening after the hack — prioritising custody security over yield and convenience.
Travel demand is still being paid for: Delta gapped +4.1%, Airbnb +4.1%, Choice Hotels raised guidance. Experience spending is proving stickier than goods spending even under budget pressure.
long_term: Security is becoming a purchased product across every domain — cyberattacks on European supermarket refrigeration show operational technology is now a consumer-facing risk, which pulls spend from IT budgets into physical-world resilience permanently.

Knowledge and productivity are being unbundled from seats and licences toward agents; public search interest in 'ai agents vs agentic ai' and 'ai agent vs chatbot' jumping 73% signals the buyer is re-learning what they are purchasing, which compresses pricing power for incumbent software during the transition.

Health is shifting from episodic treatment to continuous self-management — cold/flu self-care demand on aging demographics, anti-aging skincare growth, and continuous glucose monitoring all reflect the same substitution of patient effort for clinical visits.

Status consumption is concentrating at the top: Ferrari raising guidance on customization demand while Dollar General and Dollar Tree dominate the value-retail conversation is the clearest possible bifurcation signal.
Mobility and housing are being renegotiated rather than abandoned — DIY maintenance and home-improvement turnover (Home Depot, Masco) replace trade-up moves when financing costs stay high.

Energy security becomes a national identity issue, not an economics one — drone strikes on a UAE nuclear plant and permitting-reform pushes mean consumers and governments will pay a premium for domestically controlled electrons for a decade.

Trade relationships are being rewired around political reliability: South Africa pivoting to China and India after AGOA suspension, DP World building China-Africa lanes, and Beijing cutting cross-border payment costs all redirect decades of goods flow.
